title: Returns that say a federal audit was required, with no audit on file
question: When an organization tells the tax authority that federal money obliged it to have a single audit, is that audit in the federal clearinghouse where such audits are filed?
finding: Of 1,982 returns for years ending June 2019 to December 2024, 77 from 34 organizations answer yes to the single-audit question for a year with no audit in the clearinghouse under the organization's employer number, its name or a listed additional number. 21 of those organizations do not describe their statements as audited with a group; the City paid them $239.0 million in the years concerned, and 9 have no audit on file for any year since 2016. The largest by City money: Instituto Familiar De La Raza Inc (Jun 2021, Jun 2022, Jun 2023, Jun 2024; $49.2 million); Bayview Hunters Pt Fndtn For Comm Improv (Jun 2022, Jun 2023; $32.5 million); Providence Foundation of San Francisco (Dec 2021, Dec 2022, Dec 2023, Dec 2024; $30.2 million); Young Community Developers Inc (Dec 2024; $16.5 million). 3 say on the return itself that the required audit was not done: Bayview Hunters Pt Fndtn For Comm Improv (Jun 2023); Young Community Developers Inc (Dec 2024); Housing Rights Committee of San Francisc (Jun 2024).
how: Form 990 Part XII line 3a (was a single audit required) and 3b (was it done), latest version of each return, joined to the clearinghouse on the employer number; an audit counts for a return when its period ends inside the tax year or within 31 days after it. Audits filed under another number are looked for by exact normalised name among California auditees and in the clearinghouse list of additional employer numbers. City money is the payment-table figure spread onto the tax year. City subawards are the federal subawards the City reported for the organization with an action date inside the missing years.
limits: A missing audit is one reading of a row; others are that the box was ticked in error by the preparer (the return of a small body with no federal money sometimes says yes); the audit was filed by a parent under a different name and number (rows marked consolidated or both are listed last for that reason, and hospital systems and housing groups belong there); the audit was late and filed after 7 November 2026, the date of the clearinghouse export; or the audit was done and sent to the City but never uploaded. The screen cannot tell these apart. The audit itself, or the City department that received it, would settle each row. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
